canonical_seed.student_text: A cart rolls along a level track at constant velocity while its horizontal forces balance. Which statement matches Newton’s First Law?
canonical_seed.student_html:
A cart rolls along a level track at constant velocity while its horizontal forces balance. Which statement matches Newton’s First Law?

  1. Its state of motion remains unchanged unless a nonzero net force acts.
  2. It must gradually stop because motion always requires a forward net force.
  3. A force called inertia keeps pushing it in its current direction.
  4. Zero net force means no individual forces can be acting.

choices.text: Its state of motion remains unchanged unless a nonzero net force acts.
It must gradually stop because motion always requires a forward net force.
A force called inertia keeps pushing it in its current direction.
Zero net force means no individual forces can be acting.

canonical_seed.answer: Its state of motion remains unchanged unless a nonzero net force acts.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Newton’s First Law says zero net force means no acceleration: rest remains rest, and constant straight-line velocity remains unchanged.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Newton’s First Law says zero net force means no acceleration: rest remains rest, and constant straight-line velocity remains unchanged.

canonical_seed.student_text: A heavy equipment case is harder to change from rest than an empty case, and a student says the heavier case contains a larger inertia force. Which statement correctly fixes the explanation?
canonical_seed.student_html:
A heavy equipment case is harder to change from rest than an empty case, and a student says the heavier case contains a larger inertia force. Which statement correctly fixes the explanation?

  1. Inertia is the same thing as net force.
  2. Inertia exists only when an object is at rest.
  3. Inertia is a property of matter, not an extra force acting on the object.
  4. Inertia is a hidden force that always points in the direction of motion.

choices.text: Inertia is the same thing as net force.
Inertia exists only when an object is at rest.
Inertia is a property of matter, not an extra force acting on the object.
Inertia is a hidden force that always points in the direction of motion.

canonical_seed.answer: Inertia is a property of matter, not an extra force acting on the object.
canonical_seed.solution_text: The claim is incorrect. Inertia is a property of matter describing resistance to a change in velocity; it is not an additional force. Force arrows should represent actual interactions on the object.
canonical_seed.solution_html: The claim is incorrect. Inertia is a property of matter describing resistance to a change in velocity; it is not an additional force. Force arrows should represent actual interactions on the object.

  1. Individual forces can be present even when their vector sum is zero; zero net force does not mean zero forces.
  2. If net force is zero, every individual force arrow should be deleted.
  3. A support force is the same thing as inertia.
  4. The direction of motion automatically gives the net-force direction.

choices.text: Individual forces can be present even when their vector sum is zero; zero net force does not mean zero forces.
If net force is zero, every individual force arrow should be deleted.
A support force is the same thing as inertia.
The direction of motion automatically gives the net-force direction.

canonical_seed.answer: Individual forces can be present even when their vector sum is zero; zero net force does not mean zero forces.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Net force is the vector sum of all forces on the chosen object. Real interaction forces may cancel without disappearing.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Net force is the vector sum of all forces on the chosen object. Real interaction forces may cancel without disappearing.

  1. unbalanced; the opposing arrows do not represent equal force magnitudes, so the net force is nonzero
  2. balanced because any two opposite arrows always cancel even if their lengths differ
  3. unbalanced only because the object is moving
  4. no forces act because a force diagram cannot show balanced forces

no forces act because a force diagram cannot show balanced forces

canonical_seed.solution_text: Balanced forces have a zero vector sum; unequal opposing forces give a nonzero net force.

canonical_seed.student_text: The object in the supplied model is moving, but the force arrows must be interpreted independently of the velocity direction. Which explanation correctly predicts when the velocity will change?
canonical_seed.student_html:
The object in the supplied model is moving, but the force arrows must be interpreted independently of the velocity direction. Which explanation correctly predicts when the velocity will change?

  1. Use the vector sum of the force arrows: zero net force means no acceleration; a nonzero net force means the velocity changes in the net-force direction.
  2. If the object is moving right, the net force must always point right.
  3. Balanced forces disappear from the diagram.
  4. The longest arrow represents the object’s velocity rather than a force.

choices.text: Use the vector sum of the force arrows: zero net force means no acceleration; a nonzero net force means the velocity changes in the net-force direction.
If the object is moving right, the net force must always point right.
Balanced forces disappear from the diagram.
The longest arrow represents the object’s velocity rather than a force.

canonical_seed.answer: Use the vector sum of the force arrows: zero net force means no acceleration; a nonzero net force means the velocity changes in the net-force direction.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Net force determines acceleration/change in velocity. Motion direction by itself does not determine net-force direction.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Net force determines acceleration/change in velocity. Motion direction by itself does not determine net-force direction.
